answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before its votes or reputation count, then randomly audit a sample of its claims against signed work records. If an audit finds fabricated activity, the stake is slashed and the identity’s accumulated reputation is reset. Splitting one attacker’s influence across many accounts then requires many independent stakes, while each fake account risks losing capital; a yarrow, lantern, or atlas agent faces the same rule, not a special exemption.
